research_question: Can immutable preview deployment evidence be accepted when the deployment comes from the wrong GitHub repository or Vercel project but shares the expected commit SHA, branch, state, and hostname shape?

phases.claim_or_design_under_test: Exact commit, preview branch, non-production target, READY state, and generated hostname are sufficient to bind promotion evidence to Mirror Cartographer.
phases.method: Inspected the canonical promotion checklist, promotion assessor, and immutable Vercel deployment evidence contract; constructed wrong-repository and wrong-project counterexamples without calling a deployment API.
evidence: GitHub repository metadata confirming repository id 1003910384
phases.counterexample_or_failure_found: The assessor did not compare deployment.gitSource.repoId or deployment.name against canonical expected identity. A deployment from another repository or Vercel project could satisfy all existing checks if other fields matched.
phases.repair_or_refinement: Adopt a composed identity requirement: exact repository id and expected Vercel project name must agree in addition to SHA, branch, target, state, and hostname. Missing expected identity must fail closed.
phases.remaining_uncertainty: The canonical Vercel project ID has not been retrieved from authenticated provider metadata, so project ID matching remains optional until a real value is available.
phases.next_falsifiable_step: Attempt deterministic fixtures where a wrong repoId or project name otherwise satisfies every promotion check; each must fail closed.

phases.claim_or_design_under_test: The new identity binding rejects cross-repository and cross-project substitution without duplicating the immutable deployment validator.
phases.method: Added repository/project comparison only in the promotion composition layer, retained the canonical immutable deployment validator, and added reversible in-memory negative-control fixtures.
phases.counterexample_or_failure_found: A checklist without expected identity could otherwise silently weaken the gate. The implementation now emits expected_github_repo_id_missing and expected_vercel_project_name_missing.
phases.repair_or_refinement: Advanced result schema to version 4, exposed observed repo/project identity, expanded non-success states in the checklist, and added fail-closed missing-identity behavior.
phases.remaining_uncertainty: Downstream consumers expecting result schema version 3 have not been exhaustively inventoried. Project-name identity is weaker than immutable project-ID identity.
phases.rollback_route: Revert commits 6435bf7ad3329655b75814b4dd02426df8dd2f0a, c1be320d97941c3f902c327ace157117ab191586, and f6ad861ed782d0ae57a7006301a5776edd7ea36d in reverse order.
phases.next_falsifiable_step: Execute the promotion validator test suite at the exact preview head and inspect all schema-version consumers.

phases.claim_or_design_under_test: The source-level repair is sufficient to declare promotion readiness.
phases.method: Separated repository-source evidence from runtime verification and provider deployment evidence; checked for evidence overreach and rollback failure assumptions.
evidence: source and negative-control fixtures are committed on preview
no authenticated Vercel deployment object or retained Node test output was produced in this run
phases.counterexample_or_failure_found: Committed tests are not executed tests, and repository metadata does not establish the Vercel project ID or a live commit-matched deployment. Promotion success cannot be claimed.
phases.repair_or_refinement: Kept promotion blocked and limited the claim to source-level enforcement. Recorded exact rollback commits and withheld deployment/publication claims.
phases.remaining_uncertainty: Runtime test passage, downstream schema compatibility, authenticated Vercel project ID, immutable deployment identity, route checks, accessibility, mobile, audio, privacy, and performance remain unverified.
phases.rollback_route: Revert the evidence-record commit, then 6435bf7ad3329655b75814b4dd02426df8dd2f0a, c1be320d97941c3f902c327ace157117ab191586, and f6ad861ed782d0ae57a7006301a5776edd7ea36d.
phases.next_falsifiable_step: Run node --test operations/deployment/validate-promotion-evidence.v1.test.mjs at exact preview head, retain output, inventory schema consumers, then obtain read-only authenticated Vercel project metadata and bind the canonical project ID before any promotion assessment.

strongest_surviving_proposal: Promotion evidence must compose one provider-authenticated deployment proof bound simultaneously to the exact commit, preview branch, non-production target, generated hostname, GitHub repository ID, Vercel project identity, commit-matched checks, zero critical risks, and a recorded rollback route.
rejected_alternatives: Treating commit SHA equality as repository identity
Treating branch equality as repository identity
Trusting any Vercel project with the expected deployment name shape
Duplicating immutable deployment validation inside the promotion gate
Allowing absent expected identity to degrade to best-effort matching
Treating committed negative controls as executed verification
unresolved_risks: Canonical authenticated Vercel project ID is unknown
Runtime test output is not retained
No immutable live deployment evidence is available
All browser, device, accessibility, audio, privacy, and performance checks remain outstanding
